title: Finite rational modules over a DVR admit finite free equivariant covers
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] and let $H$ be a flat affine finitely presented group scheme over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-affine-spectrum], with group-object diagrams over this base. Put $C=A[H]=\Gamma(H,\mathcal O_H)$, with its coordinate Hopf algebra comultiplication $\Delta$ and counit $\epsilon$. A rational $H$-module is an $A$-module $M$ with an $A$-linear coaction $\rho_M:M\to M\otimes_A C$ satisfying $(\rho_M\otimes1)\rho_M=(1\otimes\Delta)\rho_M$ and $(1\otimes\epsilon)\rho_M=1_M$; tensor products are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Suppose $N$ is a rational $H$-module finitely generated as an $A$-module, meaning that some finite set of elements spans $N$. Then there exist a rational $H$-module $P$ with a finite $A$-basis and a surjective $A$-linear map $p:P\twoheadrightarrow N$ satisfying $(p\otimes1_C)\rho_P=\rho_Np$. No torsion-freeness of $N$, smoothness, connectedness, or reductivity of $H$ is assumed. The case $N=0$ is allowed.

source.place: Definition 9.2.2, Remarks 9.2.3 and 9.2.4(i), printed p.521: resolution property over separated regular Noetherian bases of dimension at most one, specialized to a DVR. Local PDF WANTED; read https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion], applied to the full affine source $H$ and target $\operatorname{Spec}A$, the coordinate module $C$ is flat over $A$. Its coalgebra identities are among the coordinate Hopf identities assumed in the statement. Since $A$ is a domain by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], multiplication by any $a\ne0$ is injective on $A$. Tensoring this injection with $C$ is injective by [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and under $A\otimes_A C\simeq C$ it is multiplication by $a$. Thus $C$ is torsion free.

Choose generators $n_1,\ldots,n_r$ of $N$. Let $F=A^r$ with standard basis $e_i$ and define $q:F\twoheadrightarrow N$ by $q(e_i)=n_i$. Give $B=F\otimes_A C$ and $D=N\otimes_A C$ the cofree coactions $\delta_B=1_F\otimes\Delta$ and $\delta_D=1_N\otimes\Delta$. These satisfy both coaction identities directly by the corresponding coalgebra identities. The map $b=q\otimes1_C:B\to D$ is equivariant by functoriality of tensor. The map $\rho_N:N\to D$ is equivariant by the coassociativity equation for $N$. Put $T=N\oplus B$, with componentwise coaction $\delta_T$, and $f:T\to D$, $f(n,z)=\rho_N(n)-b(z)$. Then $(f\otimes1_C)\delta_T=\delta_D f$, by these two equations and linearity. All tensor maps and the identification $(N\oplus B)\otimes C\simeq(N\otimes C)\oplus(B\otimes C)$ are given on pure tensors; their inverse sends the two summands through the two inclusions.

source.place: VIII, Examples 4.2(a), Aside 4.7 and section 5, printed pp.114,117; agent-written cofree pullback assembly proving the DVR case of Alper Remark 9.2.4(i), printed p.521. Local PDFs WANTED; read online.

proof.text: Let $W=\ker(f)\subseteq T$ and let $j:W\hookrightarrow T$ be inclusion. The exact sequence $0\to W\xrightarrow{j}T\xrightarrow{f}D$, tensored with flat $C$, is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]. For $w\in W$, the equation in step 2 gives $(f\otimes1_C)\delta_T(w)=\delta_D(f(w))=0$, so $\delta_T(w)\in\operatorname{im}(j\otimes1_C)$. Hence every $w\in W$ lies in the stable core $W^\circ$ of [lem-sfb-flat-coalgebra-subcomodule-core]. That node also gives $W^\circ\subseteq W$ and its restricted coaction, so $W=W^\circ$ has a coaction $\rho_W$ with $(j\otimes1_C)\rho_W=\delta_Tj$. Composing with the two projections of $T$ shows that $a:W\to N$ and $c:W\to B$ are equivariant. Thus $W$ is the actual module pullback $\{(n,z):\rho_N(n)=b(z)\}$.

source.place: VIII, Examples 4.2(a), Aside 4.7 and section 5, printed pp.114,117; agent-written cofree pullback assembly proving the DVR case of Alper Remark 9.2.4(i), printed p.521. Local PDFs WANTED; read online.

proof.text: The projection $a$ is surjective: for any $n\in N$, expand $\rho_N(n)=\sum_k x_k\otimes d_k$, choose $y_k\in F$ with $q(y_k)=x_k$, and set $z=\sum_k y_k\otimes d_k$. Then $b(z)=\rho_N(n)$ and $(n,z)\in W$. The projection $c$ is injective: if $c(n,z)=z=0$, the defining equation gives $\rho_N(n)=0$ and applying $1_N\otimes\epsilon$ gives $n=0$. These arguments use neither a splitting of $q$ nor torsion-freeness of $N$.

source.place: VIII, Examples 4.2(a), Aside 4.7 and section 5, printed pp.114,117; agent-written cofree pullback assembly proving the DVR case of Alper Remark 9.2.4(i), printed p.521. Local PDFs WANTED; read online.

proof.text: The chosen basis of $F$ identifies $B=F\otimes_A C$ with $C^r$, by $e_i\otimes d\mapsto(0,\ldots,d,\ldots,0)$ and inverse $(d_i)\mapsto\sum_i e_i\otimes d_i$. Thus $B$ is torsion free by step 1, coordinate by coordinate. Since $c:W\hookrightarrow B$ is injective, $W$ is torsion free: $aw=0$ with $a\ne0$ implies $a c(w)=0$, then $c(w)=0$, then $w=0$.

source.place: VIII, Examples 4.2(a), Aside 4.7 and section 5, printed pp.114,117; agent-written cofree pullback assembly proving the DVR case of Alper Remark 9.2.4(i), printed p.521. Local PDFs WANTED; read online.

proof.text: For each $i$ choose $w_i\in W$ with $a(w_i)=n_i$ using step 4. Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-comodule-finite-free-lattice] to the flat $A$-coalgebra $C$, the torsion-free comodule $W$, and the finite subset $\{w_1,\ldots,w_r\}$. Its hypotheses are established in steps 1, 3 and 5. It supplies a subcomodule $P\subseteq W$ containing those lifts, with a finite $A$-basis and an equivariant inclusion $u:P\hookrightarrow W$. Set $p=a\circ u$. Its image contains each $n_i$, hence all of $N$, and composition of the two coaction equations gives $(p\otimes1_C)\rho_P=\rho_Np$. These are the required data. For $N=0$ one may take $r=0$ and directly take $P=0$ with the empty basis and zero coaction.
